jurisdiction.name: Argentina
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

instruments.official_title: Decisión Administrativa 750/2023 - Mesa Interministerial sobre Inteligencia Artificial - Creación
instruments.english_title: Administrative Decision 750/2023 creating the Interministerial Roundtable on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG); Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: In force as amended. Signed 7 September 2023 (DECAD-2023-750-APN-JGM), published in Boletín Oficial No. 35251 on 8 September 2023; the decision states no specific commencement date. Articles 2-4 replaced by Decisión Administrativa 899/2024 (B.O. 24 September 2024, in force on publication), which moved the chair to the Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología of the Jefatura de Gabinete, co-coordinated with the Secretaría de Asuntos Estratégicos, and changed the member ministries. No repeal found in the InfoLEG record or the Boletín Oficial search to October 2026; no official record of the integral AI strategy it was tasked to design was found.
instruments.scope: National executive branch (Poder Ejecutivo Nacional) ministries and secretariats
instruments.summary: Creates the Mesa Interministerial sobre Inteligencia Artificial within the Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros as a cross-cutting forum on the advance and application of AI across the economy and society, within an ethical, sustainable-development and digital-transformation framework, with the purpose of designing an integral AI strategy to be applied by the national executive. As amended by Decisión Administrativa 899/2024, it is chaired by the Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología and co-coordinated with the Secretaría de Asuntos Estratégicos, and its members are the Jefatura de Gabinete and the ministries of Defence, Economy, Foreign Affairs, Health, Security, Human Capital, Justice and Deregulation; the coordinators may invite other public or private bodies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of the national executive's interministerial AI coordination body, mandated to design a national AI strategy.

instruments.official_title: Disposición 2/2023 - Recomendaciones para una Inteligencia Artificial Fiable
instruments.english_title: Provision 2/2023 approving the Recommendations for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Subsecretaría de Tecnologías de la Información, Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG); Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Approved by Disposición DI-2023-2-APN-SSTI#JGM of 1 June 2023, published in Boletín Oficial No. 35182 on 2 June 2023; art. 3 provides it applies from publication. Annex I (recommendations) and Annex II (diagram of AI project stages) published in the web edition of the Boletín Oficial. The InfoLEG record lists Ministerio de Justicia Resolución 111/2024 as a complementary norm; no repeal found. The Ministerio de Justicia 'Derecho Fácil / Ley simple' page (argentina.gob.ar/node/380497) is a plain-language explainer of this disposición, not a separate instrument.
instruments.scope: National public sector teams leading, developing, adopting or procuring AI-based innovation projects
instruments.summary: Approves the 'Recomendaciones para una Inteligencia Artificial Fiable', a manual for public-sector staff who lead, develop, adopt or specify the procurement of AI projects. It adopts the principles of the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (proportionality, safety, fairness, privacy, human oversight, transparency and explainability, accountability), stresses that responsibility for decisions stays with humans when AI executes tasks, and sets out recommendations for each stage of the AI project life cycle, with a graphic scheme of those stages in Annex II.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The national executive's main AI ethics and responsible-use guidance for public-sector AI projects.

instruments.scope: The AAIP's National Directorates of Transparency Policy Evaluation and of Personal Data Protection; the programme addresses public and private bodies that use automated decision systems
instruments.official_title: Resolución 161/2023 (RESOL-2023-161-APN-AAIP): Programa de transparencia y protección de datos personales en el uso de la Inteligencia Artificial
instruments.english_title: AAIP Resolution 161/2023 creating the Programme on Transparency and Personal Data Protection in the Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública
instruments.publisher_name: Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública
instruments.current_status: Signed by the AAIP Director (Beatriz de Anchorena) on 30 August 2023 and published in the Boletín Oficial, primera sección, on 4 September 2023 (aviso 69539/23). The 2024 AAIP AI guide cites the resolution as dated 26/08/2023; the Boletín Oficial text gives 30/08/2023. No amendment or repeal was found in the Boletín Oficial up to 11 October 2026; the AAIP programme page still presents the programme as current.
instruments.summary: Creates, within the data protection and access-to-information authority, the 'Programa de transparencia y protección de datos personales en el uso de la Inteligencia Artificial', set out in Annex IF-2023-99735227-APN-AAIP, to promote analysis, regulation and capacity-building for AI development and use in the public and private sectors. Article 2 instructs the AAIP's National Directorates of Transparency Policy Evaluation and of Personal Data Protection to run the programme jointly and set up monitoring and evaluation; the programme page lists three components: an AI observatory, governance and social participation (including a multidisciplinary advisory council), and capacity-building through good-practice guides, training and awareness campaigns.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of the data protection authority's AI work programme, under which the 2024 responsible-AI guide was produced.

instruments.official_title: Ley 25.326 de Protección de los Datos Personales
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Act (Law 25,326)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Nación Argentina (sanctioned 4 October 2000); partially promulgated by Decreto 995/2000
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force. Consolidated text on InfoLEG/argentina.gob.ar shows the last amendment by Ley 26.343 (B.O. 9 January 2008). The control body is the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública (Decreto 1558/2001 art. 29 as substituted by Decreto 899/2017). Article 20 has not been regulated. Replacement bills (executive bill 0012-PE-2023 and later proyectos) have not been enacted. The text contains no AI-specific provision.
instruments.scope: Public and private files, registers and databases of personal data in Argentina
instruments.summary: Argentina's general data protection law, protecting personal data held in public and private files, registers and databases and creating the habeas data action. It sets lawfulness, consent, data quality, security and cross-border transfer rules that govern the use of personal data to train and run AI systems. Article 20 provides that judicial decisions and administrative acts that assess human conduct may not be based solely on the result of computerised processing of personal data that defines the profile or personality of the person concerned, and that such acts are incurably void.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing AI processing of personal data; art. 20 bars judicial and administrative decisions on human conduct based solely on automated profiling.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 1558/2001 - Protección de Datos Personales - Reglamentación de la Ley N° 25.326
instruments.english_title: Decree 1558/2001 regulating the Personal Data Protection Act
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force. Amended by Decreto 1160/2010 (B.O. 13 August 2010) and Decreto 899/2017 (B.O. 6 November 2017), which made the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública the control body of Ley 25.326. The regulation of article 20 (decisions based on computerised processing) reads 'Sin reglamentar'.
instruments.scope: Data controllers and users of personal data subject to Ley 25.326
instruments.summary: Regulatory decree implementing Ley 25.326, approving in its Annex I the article-by-article regulation of the data protection law and setting a 180-day deadline for existing databases to register and comply. It details consent, data quality, access and rectification rights, registration of databases, sanctions and the control body, now the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública. Article 20 of the law, on decisions based solely on computerised processing of personal data, is left unregulated.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Implementing rules of the data protection law that governs AI processing of personal data; confirms that the automated-decision clause (art. 20) has no regulation.

instruments.official_title: Ley 27.699 - Apruébase el Protocolo Modificatorio del Convenio para la Protección de las Personas con Respecto al Tratamiento Automatizado de Datos de Carácter Personal
instruments.english_title: Law 27,699 approving the Protocol amending the Convention for the Protection of Individuals with regard to Automatic Processing of Personal Data (Convention 108+)
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Nación Argentina
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: Approval law sanctioned 9 November 2022 and published in the Boletín Oficial on 30 November 2022 (No. 35058). The law only approves the Protocol (CETS 223, Strasbourg, 10 October 2018); the date of deposit of Argentina's instrument of ratification and the Protocol's entry into force were not verified on an Argentine official source. The approval of the original Convention 108 and its Additional Protocol is a separate law, Ley 27.483 (B.O. 2 January 2019).
instruments.scope: Argentina as a party to Council of Europe Convention 108 as amended
instruments.summary: Law by which Congress approves the Protocol amending Council of Europe Convention 108 (Convention 108+), signed in Strasbourg on 10 October 2018, whose Spanish translation is annexed. The approved text gives every person the right not to be subject to a decision significantly affecting them based solely on automated processing without their views being taken into account, and the right to obtain knowledge of the reasoning underlying data processing whose results are applied to them. It also adds data breach notification and other modernised obligations for controllers.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National approval of Convention 108+, which includes a right against solely automated decisions and a right to the reasoning behind automated processing.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 70/2023 (DNU) - Bases para la Reconstrucción de la Economía Argentina
instruments.english_title: Necessity and Urgency Decree 70/2023: Bases for the Reconstruction of the Argentine Economy (AI-piloted aircraft clause)
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación, in general agreement of ministers)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: Necessity and urgency decree (DNU) dated 20 December 2023, published 21 December 2023 (B.O. No. 35326); it contains no specific commencement clause. Article 203 substituted article 79 of the Código Aeronáutico (Ley 17.285); the consolidated Código Aeronáutico on argentina.gob.ar shows art. 79 in the text given by art. 203 of Decreto 70/2023. The AI-piloted aircraft regulation the article calls for was not found.
instruments.scope: Civil aviation under the Código Aeronáutico (Ley 17.285)
instruments.summary: Omnibus necessity and urgency decree deregulating large parts of the Argentine economy, including amendments to the Código Aeronáutico (Ley 17.285). Its article 203 rewrites article 79 of the Code so that every crewed aircraft must carry a qualified pilot-in-command, the remote pilot is the commander of an uncrewed aircraft, and 'aircraft piloted by artificial intelligence shall be subject to special regulation'. This is the only explicit AI provision in the decree.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Inserts into the Aeronautical Code an explicit legal mandate for special regulation of AI-piloted aircraft.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 98/2023 - Reglamentación de la Ley N° 27.553
instruments.english_title: Decree 98/2023 regulating Law 27,553 on electronic or digital prescriptions and telehealth
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force; amended by Decreto 345/2024 (B.O. 22 April 2024), which did not change the AI clause (Annex art. 4, item k, unchanged in the consolidated text). The Ministerio de Salud is the enforcement authority (art. 2).
instruments.scope: Platforms that issue, validate or dispense electronic or digital prescriptions or manage telehealth services
instruments.summary: Decree approving the regulation of Ley 27.553 on electronic and digital prescriptions and telehealth, naming the Ministerio de Salud as enforcement authority and creating the Licencia Sanitaria Federal. Annex article 4 sets duties for prescription and telehealth platforms on data processing, security and confidentiality. Item k provides that any use of artificial intelligence must observe the restrictions imposed on it, may only support professional decision-making, and always requires supervision by health professionals.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rule limiting AI in telehealth and e-prescription platforms to decision support under professional supervision.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 159/2023 - Plataforma Digital del Sector Público Nacional. Decreto N° 87/2017. Modificación
instruments.english_title: Decree 159/2023 amending Decree 87/2017 to add the 'TINA' AI chatbot to the National Public Sector Digital Platform
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: Published in the Boletín Oficial on 22 March 2023 (No. 35135). No modifying norms are listed on InfoLEG. Whether the TINA chatbot is still operated was not checked.
instruments.scope: Agencies and jurisdictions of the National Public Sector covered by Decreto 87/2017; provinces, CABA and municipalities invited to adhere
instruments.summary: Decree adding the State chatbot 'TINA' to the National Public Sector Digital Platform and making it the official conversational channel of the national State. Its recitals describe TINA, set up under Resolución 14/2022 of the Secretaría de Innovación Pública, as an AI tool that automates tasks through natural-language conversation. Article 2 lists its minimum functions, including information on procedures, online transactions linked to Mi Argentina, proactive messages and referral to human operators for matters needing a person; provinces, CABA and municipalities are invited to adhere.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Decree establishing an AI chatbot as an official national government service channel, including referral to human operators.

instruments.official_title: Ley 27.506 - Régimen de Promoción de la Economía del Conocimiento
instruments.english_title: Law 27,506: Knowledge Economy Promotion Regime
instruments.issuing_authority: Congreso de la Nación Argentina
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force; substantially amended by Ley 27.570 (B.O. 26 October 2020) and Decreto 679/2022 (B.O. 11 October 2022). Under art. 20 as substituted by Ley 27.570 the regime runs until 31 December 2029. The AI reference in art. 2(i) is unchanged in the consolidated text.
instruments.scope: Companies carrying out promoted knowledge-economy activities that register in the Registro Nacional de Beneficiarios
instruments.summary: Law creating a promotion regime with tax and contribution benefits for knowledge-economy companies such as software, audiovisual production, biotechnology and professional services. Article 2(i) lists among the promoted activities the manufacture, set-up, maintenance and introduction of goods and services for production automation characterised by industry 4.0 technologies 'such as artificial intelligence, robotics and industrial internet'. Beneficiaries must register and meet employment, export or R&D requirements.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding incentive law naming AI-based automation as an eligible promoted activity.

instruments.official_title: Decreto 749/2024 - Apruébase Reglamentación del Título VII - Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI) - Ley Nº 27.742
instruments.english_title: Decree 749/2024 regulating the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI) of Law 27,742
instruments.issuing_authority: Poder Ejecutivo Nacional (Presidencia de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio de Justicia (InfoLEG, Información Legislativa y Documental)
instruments.current_status: In force; amended several times, most recently by Decreto 748/2026 (B.O. 18 August 2026) and Decreto 868/2026 (B.O. 4 September 2026) per the consolidated-text notes. The technology-sector definition naming AI was restated by art. 2 of Decreto 105/2026 (B.O. 19 February 2026), which also extended the RIGI adhesion deadline by one year. A separate 'Super RIGI' bill for new industries including AI (0005-PE-2026) passed the Cámara de Diputados on 24 June 2026 and is pending in the Senado.
instruments.scope: Investors in large projects adhering to the RIGI under Title VII of Ley 27.742
instruments.summary: Decree approving the regulation of the Large Investment Incentive Regime (RIGI) created by Title VII of Ley 27.742 (Ley Bases), which grants tax, customs and foreign-exchange benefits and regulatory stability to large investment projects. Annex article 3 defines the eligible sectors; the technology sector covers innovative production of goods and services in fields including biotechnology, the software industry, robotics and artificial intelligence. It sets the procedures and evaluation of adhesion applications.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding investment-incentive regulation that names AI as an eligible technology sector.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 111/2024 - Programa Nacional Integral de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia - Créase
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Justice Resolution 111/2024 creating the Comprehensive National Programme on Artificial Intelligence in Justice
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Justicia
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 9 April 2024 (RESOL-2024-111-APN-MJ), published in the Boletín Oficial on 11 April 2024. Art. 8 replaced by Res. MJ 116/2024 (B.O. 11 April 2024) to order publication; art. 1 replaced and art. 7 repealed by Res. MJ 149/2024 (B.O. 7 May 2024), which placed the programme under the Dirección Nacional del Sistema Argentino de Información Jurídica (Secretaría de Justicia). Referred to as in force by Res. MJ 469/2026 (September 2026).
instruments.scope: Ministerio de Justicia; AI projects in the Ministry and the justice system
instruments.summary: Creates the Programa Nacional Integral de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia to promote the use of AI to improve administrative procedures and judicial processes, ensuring respect for fundamental rights, and citing Disposición 2/2023 and the UNESCO AI ethics recommendation. The programme is run by a coordinator with an ad honorem advisory committee chaired by the Minister, and must present an annual plan covering prior impact assessments and audits before any AI deployment in the Ministry or the justice system, AI projects, AI risk control, training on AI ethics for the Ministry and the national judiciary, and stakeholder meetings.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level AI governance programme for the justice sector, with impact-assessment and risk-control planning duties.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 469/2026 - Mesa Estratégica de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia (MEIAJ) - Creación
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Justice Resolution 469/2026 creating the Strategic Roundtable on Artificial Intelligence in Justice
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Justicia
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 21 September 2026 (RESOL-2026-469-APN-MJ), published in the Boletín Oficial on 23 September 2026. The MEIAJ must submit a preliminary Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia within 90 days of its first meeting (art. 10); no strategy had been published by 11 October 2026.
instruments.scope: Ministerio de Justicia units; invited representatives of the judiciary, public prosecutors, provinces, universities and others
instruments.summary: Creates the Mesa Estratégica de Inteligencia Artificial en la Justicia (MEIAJ) in the Ministry of Justice's Unidad Gabinete de Asesores to help draft an AI Strategy for the Justice system, following technical assistance from the EU's EL PACCTO 2.0 programme and the French École nationale de la magistrature. Its functions include mapping existing AI initiatives, identifying priorities, proposing principles, pilot use cases, training and indicators, and submitting a preliminary strategy within 90 days of its first meeting. Article 7 states the strategy is a planning and coordination instrument, not a general AI regulatory regime, and must respect data protection, information security, intellectual property and transparency rules and promote human oversight, traceability and risk assessment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sets up the body that will draft a justice-sector AI strategy and fixes its guiding safeguards.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 710/2024 - Unidad de Inteligencia Artificial Aplicada a la Seguridad (UIAAS) - Creación
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Security Resolution 710/2024 creating the Artificial Intelligence Unit Applied to Security
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Seguridad
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 26 July 2024 (RESOL-2024-710-APN-MSG), published in the Boletín Oficial on 29 July 2024. No amendment or repeal found in the Boletín Oficial search to October 2026.
instruments.scope: Ministerio de Seguridad and the federal police and security forces
instruments.summary: Creates the Unidad de Inteligencia Artificial Aplicada a la Seguridad (UIAAS) in the Ministry of Security's Dirección de Ciberdelito y Asuntos Cibernéticos, headed by that director and staffed by representatives of the federal police and security forces, with the mission of preventing, detecting, investigating and prosecuting crime using AI. Its listed functions include patrolling open social networks, apps and the dark web, real-time analysis of security-camera images with facial recognition, machine-learning analysis of historical crime data to predict future crimes, cyber-threat detection, drone surveillance, and detection of suspicious financial transactions. The unit must adapt its functions to the cyber-patrolling guidelines of Resolución 428/2024.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ministry-level instrument authorising police use of AI, including facial recognition and predictive policing.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 428/2024 - Pautas, principios, criterios, recomendaciones y directivas para las labores preventivas de los delitos que se desarrollan en ambientes cibernéticos
instruments.english_title: Ministry of Security Resolution 428/2024 on guidelines for preventive police work on crimes in cyberspace (open-source cyber-patrolling)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministerio de Seguridad
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 27 May 2024 (RESOL-2024-428-APN-MSG), published in the Boletín Oficial on 28 May 2024. Cited as in force by Res. MSG 710/2024. No amendment or repeal found in the Boletín Oficial search to October 2026.
instruments.scope: Federal police and security forces
instruments.summary: Sets the rules federal police and security forces must follow when carrying out preventive work on crimes in cyberspace, limited to publicly accessible websites and open digital sources, with data-protection limits under Ley 25.326, a ban on processing sensitive data and minors' posts without judicial authorisation, and the deletion of data when no case is opened. Article 5 provides that the use of software or tools for automated information processing based on artificial intelligence, machine learning, expert systems, neural networks, deep learning or future techniques must be limited to the strict needs of the regulated activity and supervised by the Ministry of Security.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rule on police use of AI tools in open-source online surveillance (art. 5).

instruments.official_title: Resolución 197/2026 - Guía de Controles Inteligencia Artificial - SIGEN
instruments.english_title: SIGEN Resolution 197/2026 approving the Artificial Intelligence Controls Guide
instruments.issuing_authority: Sindicatura General de la Nación
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina; Sindicatura General de la Nación
instruments.current_status: Signed 16 June 2026 (RESOL-2026-197-APN-SIGEN), published in the Boletín Oficial on 22 June 2026. Art. 2 makes the Guide applicable to the whole Sector Público Nacional (art. 8, Ley 24.156). The annex (IF-2026-53068261-APN-GPNYPT#SIGEN) is not printed in the Boletín Oficial; the notice points to the PDF on argentina.gob.ar.
instruments.scope: Entire national public sector as defined in art. 8 of Ley 24.156
instruments.summary: Approves the Guía de Controles Inteligencia Artificial, a risk-based internal-control guide that applies to the whole national public sector and gives government auditors an updated review programme for AI. It covers two modes: individual use of generative AI tools by public servants (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini), requiring an institutional AI-use policy, approval by the IT unit with legal review of terms and conditions, documentation and human review of AI-assisted outputs, and controls against exposing non-public or personal data; and AI systems embedded in organisational processes, including algorithm training. It stresses that accountability stays with officials and requires traceability of automated decisions and effective human oversight.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Mandatory internal-control and audit framework for AI and generative-AI use across the national public sector.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 282/2025 - Lineamientos Estratégicos en Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología 2025-2027
instruments.english_title: Resolution 282/2025 approving the Strategic Guidelines on Innovation, Science and Technology 2025-2027
instruments.issuing_authority: Secretaría de Innovación, Ciencia y Tecnología, Jefatura de Gabinete de Ministros
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 30 October 2025 (RESOL-2025-282-APN-SICYT#JGM), published in the Boletín Oficial on 31 October 2025 and in force from publication (art. 2); annex IF-2025-120923065-APN-SSCYT#JGM published in the web edition. Not an AI-specific strategy; no standalone national AI plan or strategy of the 2024-2026 administration was found in the Boletín Oficial.
instruments.scope: National science, technology and innovation system; national public sector digital services
instruments.summary: Approves the 2025-2027 strategic guidelines for innovation, science and technology, framed by the Plan Nacional de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación 2030 (Ley 27.738), prioritising agroindustry, mining and energy, health and the knowledge economy. Artificial intelligence is named first among the four high-impact cross-cutting technologies, with AI and data science to be particularly encouraged through 'evolving, non-restrictive regulatory frameworks', and the guidelines call for promoting AI adoption in the national State to optimise public management.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national S&T strategy naming AI a priority enabling technology and signalling a light-touch regulatory stance.

instruments.official_title: Resolución 16/2024 (DGA) - Comité de Innovación sobre Inteligencia Artificial - Creación
instruments.english_title: Customs Directorate-General Resolution 16/2024 creating the Innovation Committee on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Dirección General de Aduanas, Administración Federal de Ingresos Públicos
instruments.publisher_name: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
instruments.current_status: Signed 17 May 2024 (RESOL-2024-16-E-AFIP-DGADUA), published in the Boletín Oficial on 20 May 2024. AFIP was later replaced by the Agencia de Recaudación y Control Aduanero (ARCA); no repeal of this resolution was found in the Boletín Oficial search.
instruments.scope: Customs service (Dirección General de Aduanas)
instruments.summary: Creates, within the customs directorate of the federal revenue agency, the Comité de Innovación sobre Inteligencia Artificial to coordinate technical, operational and IT areas and foreign-trade stakeholders in proposing how to implement AI as a tool supporting customs work, in line with AFIP's 2022-2025 strategic plan on data analytics and AI. The committee is chaired by the customs directorate, adopts its own rules, may form multidisciplinary working groups and invite business chambers, public bodies and universities, and submits recommendations to customs management.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Agency-level AI governance body for the tax and customs administration.

instruments.official_title: Resolución PGN 14/2025 - Programa de Inteligencia Artificial del Ministerio Público Fiscal de la Nación
instruments.english_title: Attorney General Resolution 14/2025 creating the Artificial Intelligence Programme of the National Public Prosecution Service
instruments.issuing_authority: Procuración General de la Nación (Ministerio Público Fiscal de la Nación)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministerio Público Fiscal de la Nación
instruments.current_status: Signed 14 May 2025 and published on the Ministerio Público Fiscal resolutions site. Cited as in force by Res. PGN 64/2026. The date is the resolution date; the MPF publishes its resolutions on its own site, not in the Boletín Oficial.
instruments.scope: Ministerio Público Fiscal de la Nación
instruments.summary: Creates a Programa de Inteligencia Artificial within the national Public Prosecution Service to develop a strategic and comprehensive approach to incorporating AI, run by the Secretaría de Coordinación Institucional. Its functions are to design an institutional AI strategy, propose guidelines, technical standards and ethical principles for the design, acquisition, implementation, evaluation and use of AI tools, receive and assess units' AI projects and their impact, draft protocols and good-practice guides, monitor projects and promote training and cooperation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of the national prosecution service's AI governance programme.

instruments.summary: Approves binding interpretive criteria for the Personal Data Protection Law 25.326. instruments.summary: Sets the BCRA's minimum requirements for governing and managing technology and information-security risk at financial entities, and includes a dedicated section 4.6 on artificial intelligence and machine learning. Entities must document why they use AI or ML software, directly or through third parties, assign roles, identify the models, algorithms and datasets, and set metrics and thresholds for reliability; risk analyses must cover model training and drift, training data, privacy and consumer impact, and testing maturity. They must also put in place bias and anti-discrimination measures, documentation on transparency, explainability and interpretability, periodic reviews against risk tolerance, and notice to customers when services use these technologies; the board must ensure impact assessments and risk appetites are set for AI use.
